_schema.purpose: Plain-language translation layer for healer alerts. Render-time lookup keyed by (source, subject); on match, surface severity + summary + recommended_action above a collapsed technical-detail footer. See docs/runbooks/add-new-healer-alert.md.
_schema.lookup_rule: Exact match on subject first; if miss, strip trailing ':'-segments from subject one at a time and retry. First match wins (longest-prefix). If the ':'-prefix-strip also misses, strip a trailing '-YYYY-MM-DD' ISO-date suffix from the subject and retry once, so a stable prefix key (e.g. 'weekly', 'check-i') matches a date-rotating subject like 'weekly-2026-06-15' (the stripped key must differ from the original AND exist under the source). If exact + ':'-prefix-strip + ISO-date-strip all miss, a source-level '*' catch-all entry (when present) matches any subject under that source. Source must match exactly.
_schema.severity_note: Display-only label, decoupled from the producer's queue severity ('warning' | 'critical'). URGENT does NOT imply queue severity='critical' — it's the operator-facing urgency.
_schema.tier_note: Operator-triage gradient (spec: agents/beacon/specs/operator-ux-alert-taxonomy.md). NOW = blocks the chain right now, requires immediate action. SOON = needs attention within hours. FYI = informational, no action required. Conservative classification — when uncertain, lean toward FYI rather than NOW. Unknown subjects (not in this table) default to SOON in the renderer per spec § 2.
_schema.stopgap_note: Translation layer is a stopgap until the Pulse cycle upgrade (follow-up to PR #108) ships healer-alert triage as a core Pulse responsibility. Once Pulse triages, this table can retire; the CI gate that enforces every healer has an entry stays useful as an ergonomics review trigger.
_schema.never_silence_note: Optional per-entry boolean. By default a (source, subject) present in this table is a known pattern that Check 0 (alert_triage_state.classify) Tier-3-silences to digest. Set never_silence: true on an entry to keep its plain-language translation but force it to surface (Tier 4, route=escalate) instead of being muted — for detections like a dark pulse check, where the translation makes the alert clearer but silencing it would defeat the watcher's whole purpose.

sequence-paused.plain_language_summary: A build-sequence stopped itself because two records disagreed and it refused to guess. The most common cause is a gate-mismatch: a step PR merged on GitHub (the work is done) but the chain pipeline never recorded the merge event -- usually a merge that bypassed the auto-merge / REVIEW_PASS path, or a dropped chain-event. The pause is the safety brake: the advancer will not re-dispatch already-merged work, nor advance downstream steps on an unconfirmed merge. The exact pause reason (gate-mismatch, stranded step, or schema-validation) is in the technical-detail footer below.
sequence-paused.recommended_action: Read the pause reason in the raw message. For a gate-mismatch (chain_merged=False, gh_merged=True): verify the step PR actually merged (gh pr view <#>), then reconcile and resume -- `skip sequence <seq_id> step <step-id>` marks the step merged without forcing the chain to re-observe it, then `resume sequence <seq_id>`. Do NOT `retry` (rebuilds already-merged work) or `cancel` (discards a healthy sequence). For a stranded-step or schema-validation pause, fix the underlying issue named in the reason, then `resume`. Producer: scripts/build_sequence_advancer.py.

doorbell.plain_language_summary: The doorbell notifier already DMs you directly on the doorbell channel the moment it fires, so by the time Pulse triages this alert the message is in your Telegram thread. A second Pulse-side escalation would just duplicate it, and treating it as novel resets the triage tier on every emit. Surfaced here only for the digest record.
doorbell.recommended_action: None at the Pulse layer — the doorbell notifier chat_id DM is the primary delivery and is already in your thread. Producer: scripts/doorbell_notifier.py; payload carries intent=doorbell + chat_id (subject is None, so this matches via the intent fallback).

medic-silenced-needs-fix.plain_language_summary: Medic durably silenced a confirmed false-positive alert so it stops looping in your inbox — but Medic can only quiet the symptom, not patch the code. The underlying bug is still unfixed. This one-time notice carries the root cause and what to fix at the source; it will not repeat (the silence is the dedupe).
medic-silenced-needs-fix.recommended_action: Apply the root-cause fix named in the alert body (the healer/source that emits the silenced fingerprint). Once shipped, lift the mask with `larry_alerts.unsilence("<fingerprint>")` so a genuine future recurrence isn't hidden. Audit trail: medic-dispatcher.log; ledger classification=reversible.

medic-diagnosis.plain_language_summary: Medic ran an autonomous diagnosis and already delivered its findings to you directly via a chat_id DM. By the time Pulse triages this alert the DM is in your Telegram thread, so a second Pulse-side escalation would just duplicate it. Surfaced here only for the digest record.
medic-diagnosis.recommended_action: None at the Pulse layer — the medic chat_id DM is the primary delivery and is already in your thread. If the diagnosed condition stays unresolved, Medic re-escalates via its own chat_id path. Producer: medic module; payload carries intent=medic-diagnosis + chat_id.

heal-pipeline-stall:pipeline-stall:unrou.plain_language_summary: The Medic relay failed to deliver a duplicate of an underlying heal-pipeline-stall:pipeline-stall:unrouted-pr alert that outbox-notifier ALREADY delivered to you via route=escalate. medic-dispatcher counts Medic's deliberate no-op (Medic ran but emitted no source=medic notification for this known stall) as a delivery failure and wraps it as a relay-failure alert. There is no Pulse-layer action — the underlying alert is already in your thread; this is surfaced only for the digest record.
heal-pipeline-stall:pipeline-stall:unrou.recommended_action: None at the Pulse layer — the underlying heal-pipeline-stall:pipeline-stall:unrouted-pr alert was already delivered route=escalate. If medic-dispatcher relay failures recur for genuinely-undelivered alerts (where Medic is the sole delivery path), investigate run_medic.sh + the operator allowlist. G-rule: medic-dispatcher-delivery-failure-tier4-001.

heal-pipeline-stall:pipeline-stall:no-se.plain_language_summary: The Medic relay failed to deliver a duplicate of an underlying heal-pipeline-stall:pipeline-stall:no-session-revision alert that outbox-notifier ALREADY delivered to you via route=escalate. medic-dispatcher counts Medic's deliberate no-op (Medic ran but emitted no source=medic notification for this known stall) as a delivery failure and wraps it as a relay-failure alert. There is no Pulse-layer action — the underlying alert is already in your thread; this is surfaced only for the digest record.
heal-pipeline-stall:pipeline-stall:no-se.recommended_action: None at the Pulse layer — the underlying heal-pipeline-stall:pipeline-stall:no-session-revision alert was already delivered route=escalate. If medic-dispatcher relay failures recur for genuinely-undelivered alerts (where Medic is the sole delivery path), investigate run_medic.sh + the operator allowlist. G-rule: medic-dispatcher-delivery-failure-tier4-001.

pipeline-stall:forge-no-pr.plain_language_summary: Forge finished a build but the PR never opened. The branch was pushed (or at least built) but `gh pr create` failed silently — the chain stalled because Mirror has nothing to review.
pipeline-stall:forge-no-pr.recommended_action: Check ~/agent-worktrees/wt-forge-<task_id>/ for the branch state and ~/agents/logs/inbox_watcher.log around the alert timestamp for the gh error. If the branch is pushed, run `gh pr create` manually from the worktree. Runbook: runbooks/heal-pipeline-stall.md.

pipeline-stall:marker-invisible.plain_language_summary: Mirror finished a review but the outbox-notifier never parsed her marker — the verdict block was wrapper-shaped or inline-prefix shaped instead of canonical `=== REVIEW_PASS ===` / `=== REVIEW_REVISION ===`. The chain stalled because the verdict is invisible to the dispatcher.
pipeline-stall:marker-invisible.recommended_action: Open the Mirror session for the named task and re-emit the verdict via `scripts/marker.py render mirror <type>`. Don't hand-type marker blocks. Runbook: runbooks/heal-pipeline-stall.md (marker-invisible section).

pipeline-stall:no-session-revision.plain_language_summary: A REVIEW_REVISION verdict dispatched a revision back to Forge but didn't carry a `--resume <session_id>` — Forge will start fresh with no context from the original build session, which usually means re-solving the same problem.
pipeline-stall:no-session-revision.recommended_action: Check the notifier session at ~/agents/logs/outbox_notifier.log around the alert timestamp for the missing session_id. Re-dispatch the revision with the original session_id pulled from inbox-watcher's session log, or accept the cold-start cost. Runbook: runbooks/heal-pipeline-stall.md.

pipeline-stall:retry-exhausted.plain_language_summary: The MAX_RETRIES loop in agent_runner.py burned through every attempt for this task without success. The chain stopped because retrying further would just hit the same wall — likely a stuck premise, missing dependency, or upstream blocker.
pipeline-stall:retry-exhausted.recommended_action: Read ~/agents/logs/<agent>.log filtered to the named task_id to find the recurring failure mode. Either fix the upstream issue and re-dispatch, or REJECT the task from the inbox with a reason. Runbook: runbooks/heal-pipeline-stall.md.

pipeline-stall:tier2-fallback-failed-rat.plain_language_summary: Tier 1 (agent Claude Max account) hit a rate-limit AND the Tier 2 fallback (HOME-swap to /home/larry/.claude-larry-personal) also failed. Both accounts are limited or one of them has stale credentials.
pipeline-stall:tier2-fallback-failed-rat.recommended_action: Wait for Tier 1's reset window (the original CLI error gives the time). If Tier 2 should have worked, audit credentials per docs/runbooks/restore-larry-personal-claude-oauth-tier2.md. The chain is paused on this task; it will not auto-recover.

pipeline-stall:tier2-fallback-unavailabl.plain_language_summary: Tier 1 OAuth hit a 401 (expired refresh token) AND the Tier 2 fallback directory at /home/larry/.claude-larry-personal is missing or unprovisioned. The chain is stuck — no working account to retry against.
pipeline-stall:tier2-fallback-unavailabl.recommended_action: Run `python3 scripts/auth_orchestrator.py` to re-authenticate Tier 1, OR `python3 scripts/auth_orchestrator_tier2.py` to provision Tier 2. Full recovery steps: docs/runbooks/restore-larry-personal-claude-oauth-tier2.md.

pipeline-stall:tier2-fallback-skipped-ra.plain_language_summary: Tier 1 hit a rate-limit and the Tier 2 fallback was SKIPPED (short-circuited, not attempted) because Tier 2 OAuth is known-expired or unprovisioned. Same underlying state as tier2-fallback-failed-rate_limit, surfaced before the HOME-swap rather than after a failed attempt. Informational: the task waits for Tier 1s rolling-5h window to reset on its own.
pipeline-stall:tier2-fallback-skipped-ra.recommended_action: None required for the immediate stall — Tier 1 auto-recovers when its rolling-5h reset window cycles. To restore the Tier 2 safety net for next time, re-auth per docs/runbooks/restore-larry-personal-claude-oauth-tier2.md. Runbook: runbooks/heal-pipeline-stall.md.

pipeline-stall:tier2-fallback-skipped-au.plain_language_summary: Tier 1 OAuth hit a 401 (expired refresh token) and the Tier 2 fallback was SKIPPED (short-circuited, not attempted) because the Tier 2 directory is missing or unprovisioned. Same root cause as tier2-fallback-unavailable-auth_401, surfaced as a pre-attempt skip rather than an unavailable-after-attempt. Informational; the chain pauses on this task until an account is re-authed.
pipeline-stall:tier2-fallback-skipped-au.recommended_action: Re-auth Tier 1 via python3 scripts/auth_orchestrator.py, or provision Tier 2 via python3 scripts/auth_orchestrator_tier2.py. Full recovery steps: docs/runbooks/restore-larry-personal-claude-oauth-tier2.md.

pipeline-stall:pr-create-inferred-failur.plain_language_summary: A preflight/clarify task pointer was consumed but its archived outbox shows no PR (exit_code != 0 / error / auth_401), so the healer INFERRED a PR-create failure and routed it to this distinct lower-urgency subject (own cooldown) rather than the URGENT forge-no-pr build-gap alarm. In practice this is almost always a FALSE ALARM on a source=larry task: the source=larry outbox path does not populate `pr_url` after the PR is actually created, so a clarify pointer whose sibling build already shipped looks like a loss. The translation layer cannot tell a false alarm from a genuine source=forge infra crash because it keys only on (healer-source, subject), so this is conservatively classified FYI with a verify-first action.
pipeline-stall:pr-create-inferred-failur.recommended_action: Verify before acting: check whether the sibling build PR for this task family already merged (gh pr list --search <task-family>, or the Missions tab). If it shipped, this is the known source=larry pr_url-unset artifact -- no action. ONLY if there is genuinely no sibling PR AND the archived outbox (~/agents/outboxes/forge/.archive/<task>.json) shows a real infra/auth crash before PR-create is a re-dispatch warranted. Root-cause fix is healer-side (populate pr_url on the source=larry outbox path, or extend _preflight_family_shipped correlation); this translation is a stopgap. Runbook: runbooks/heal-pipeline-stall.md.

pipeline-stall:unrouted-pr.plain_language_summary: An open PR has no Mirror review-request logged — an externally-authored PR skipped the notifier's auto-dispatch, so Mirror won't review it until you route it manually.
pipeline-stall:unrouted-pr.recommended_action: Route it from Beacon chat: `dispatch mirror review pr=<url>` (the raw alert below carries the exact PR URL and a routing-events tail to verify it fired).

stalled-pending-sequence.plain_language_summary: A build-sequence is still `pending` with an unresolved Mirror DAG-preflight REVISION older than 30 min. Mirror sent a REVISION back through the Beacon notify path, but Beacon never amended-and-re-dispatched (mechanical DAG fix) nor escalated it to you (scope/spec problem). The sequence is wedged — no step has kicked off.
stalled-pending-sequence.recommended_action: Open the named sequence at ~/agents/blackboard/build-sequences/<seq-id>.json and read its audit_log: the `dag-preflight-revision-routed` entry shows when Mirror's REVISION arrived. Check Beacon's inbox/session for the `notify-dag-revision-<seq-id>` task — if Beacon stalled mid-handle, resume it; if the verdict is a scope/spec problem it should have escalated, so decide the binary yourself and either amend the sequence (add the missing depends_on edge) and re-dispatch DAG-preflight, or REJECT the sequence. Runbook: runbooks/heal-pipeline-stall.md.

pipeline-stall:mirror-pass-unmerged.plain_language_summary: A PR earned a Mirror REVIEW_PASS but has not merged yet, so heal-pipeline-stall flagged it. The healer already routes this as escalate and DMs you directly, so by the time Pulse triages it the message is in your Telegram thread. A second Pulse-side escalation would just duplicate it. Surfaced here only for the digest record.
pipeline-stall:mirror-pass-unmerged.recommended_action: None at the Pulse layer -- the heal-pipeline-stall escalate DM is the primary delivery and is already in your thread. If the PR stays unmerged the healer re-escalates via its own route=escalate path. Runbook: runbooks/heal-pipeline-stall.md.

install-healed.plain_language_summary: A systemd unit was shipped in the repo but missing from /etc/systemd/system/; the healer installed it, daemon-reloaded, and confirmed it is running. No action needed — surfaced for the record.
install-healed.recommended_action: None — the unit was installed and verified active. Self-healed; details appear in the daily digest.

stuck-timer-healed.plain_language_summary: A systemd timer had lost its next-fire anchor and the healer restarted it (daemon-reload + restart); it is firing on schedule again. No action needed — surfaced for the record.
stuck-timer-healed.recommended_action: None — the timer was restarted and verified. Self-healed; details appear in the daily digest.

content-healed.plain_language_summary: A systemd unit's installed copy under /etc/systemd/system/ had drifted from the repo; the healer re-copied it, daemon-reloaded, and (for a long-running daemon) restarted it so the new content is live. No action needed — surfaced for the record.
content-healed.recommended_action: None — already reconciled; verify with `systemctl status <unit>`. Self-healed; details appear in the daily digest. Runbook: runbooks/heal-systemd-install-drift.md.

install-resolved.plain_language_summary: An earlier 🔴 install-drift alert for this unit has CLEARED — the unit is now installed under /etc/systemd/system/ and the stale alert line was retracted from the queue. This is the stand-down for a 🔴 you may have already seen on your phone: the drift reconciled (the post-merge install completed, or it was fixed out-of-band). No action needed.
install-resolved.recommended_action: None — stand down. The unit is installed and the prior alert is retracted; confirm with `systemctl status <unit>` if you want. Runbook: runbooks/heal-systemd-install-drift.md.

install-drift.plain_language_summary: A systemd unit is shipped in the repo's `systemd/` directory but is NOT installed at /etc/systemd/system/, and the healer could NOT auto-install it (auto-remediation is disabled for this class, or the install attempt failed). The unit isn't running on this droplet — whatever it does (a daemon, a timer, a healer) is silently absent until you install it by hand.
install-drift.recommended_action: Run `sudo cp systemd/<unit-name> /etc/systemd/system/ && sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl enable --now <unit-name>` from the repo root. Verify with `systemctl status <unit-name>`. Runbook: runbooks/heal-systemd-install-drift.md.

stuck-timer.plain_language_summary: A systemd timer momentarily read with no next-fire anchor (`NextElapseUSecRealtime` empty + `NextElapseUSecMonotonic=infinity`) and the healer restarted it. In practice this is almost always a FALSE ALARM: the anchor blanks for a sub-second while a timer fires at the top of its period, and if a `daemon-reload` lands in that exact window (as this healer's own run does at 00:00/12:00) the timer gets snapshotted anchor-less. It was never actually stuck — it keeps firing on schedule. NOTE: this is NOT an OnUnitActiveSec problem; it hits OnCalendar timers too, so converting timer types does not fix it (8fe7bef tried that and it recurred).
stuck-timer.recommended_action: None — the timer is healthy. Confirm with `systemctl show <unit> --property=NextElapseUSecRealtime,LastTriggerUSec`; a recent LastTrigger means it is firing fine. The detector now ignores timers that fired within the last ~2 minutes, so this transient should stop alerting. Treat as real only if a timer's LastTrigger is genuinely stale (older than its interval). Runbook: runbooks/heal-systemd-install-drift.md.

auto-restarted.plain_language_summary: The healer detected a long-running daemon executing older code than its on-disk script (the script's mtime was newer than the unit's active-since), and auto-restarted it so the new code is now live. No action needed — a routine self-heal success surfaced for the record only.
auto-restarted.recommended_action: None -- the daemon was restarted onto the new code and verified live. Self-healed; details appear in the daily digest. Runbook: runbooks/heal-stale-daemon-code.md.

auto-restart-failed.plain_language_summary: The healer issued `sudo systemctl restart` on a stale daemon, then checked the unit only 3s later and found it still inactive, so it escalated `auto-restart-failed:<service>`. But the 3s check window is shorter than the service's real startup latency — systemd's own restart policy (RestartSec=10 + `After=` ordering deps) brings the unit back within ~90s. In all 3 observed cases (all ourliberty-outbox-notifier.service, iters ~2704/~2947/~3000) the service self-recovered and Medic confirmed it live. A timing-window false alarm, not a genuine restart failure.
auto-restart-failed.recommended_action: None — systemd self-heals within ~90s via RestartSec + ordering deps; Medic confirms recovery every time. Surfaced for the digest record only. NOTE: this silences ONLY the `auto-restart-failed:` prefix (a check-timing artifact). The separate `still-stale-after-restart:` subject is a genuine ask-then-do (service running with OLD code after restart) and is intentionally NOT silenced. Runbook: runbooks/heal-stale-daemon-code.md.

rebound.plain_language_summary: A Telegram bot's claude config file mount had gone read-only (the file was atomically replaced on the host after the unit started, so the bot was failing with `[claude exit 1]` and looked offline). The healer restarted the unit to re-bind the current file and confirmed it is writable again. No action needed — a routine self-heal surfaced for the record only.
rebound.recommended_action: None — the bot was restarted and re-verified writable. Self-healed; details appear in the daily digest. Runbook: runbooks/claude-json-bind-drift.md.

repair-failed.plain_language_summary: A Telegram bot's claude config file mount went read-only (EROFS) and the healer tried to fix it by restarting the unit, but the restart did NOT bring the bot back. The bot is likely still offline or replying with `[claude exit 1]`, and there is no automatic retry.
repair-failed.recommended_action: Restart the unit by hand (`sudo systemctl restart <unit>`) and check `journalctl -u <unit> -n 50` for why it failed to come up. Runbook: runbooks/claude-json-bind-drift.md.

still-dangled.plain_language_summary: A bot's claude config file mount went read-only again within minutes of an automatic restart — the auto-repair fired recently and the problem came right back, so the healer stopped restarting to avoid a loop. This points at a structural problem: the read-write carve-out may have been removed from the unit file, or something is replacing the config file every few minutes.
still-dangled.recommended_action: Confirm the carve-out is still present (`systemctl cat <unit> | grep ReadWritePaths`), then restart by hand (`sudo systemctl restart <unit>`) and investigate what is replacing the file. Runbook: runbooks/claude-json-bind-drift.md.

probe-blind.plain_language_summary: The healer that fixes read-only claude-config mounts cannot probe a bot's mount namespace (its `sudo -n` / `nsenter` access failed). The healer is BLIND for that unit — if its config mount goes read-only, it will NOT be auto-repaired and the bot will look offline until someone restarts it by hand.
probe-blind.recommended_action: Fix the droplet sudoers NOPASSWD contract for nsenter and confirm `nsenter` (util-linux) is installed, so the healer can probe and auto-repair again. Runbook: runbooks/claude-json-bind-drift.md.

credential-drift:MISSING_REGISTRY_ENTRY.plain_language_summary: A credential exists on disk (e.g., a token file, OAuth refresh token, API key) but has no entry in config/token-rotation-schedule.json. It's invisible to rotation tracking — when it expires, it will silently die instead of being rotated on schedule.
credential-drift:MISSING_REGISTRY_ENTRY.recommended_action: Add an entry to config/token-rotation-schedule.json for the named credential per the existing entries' shape (4-artifact discipline: registry + runbook + calendar event + drift-healer awareness). Runbook: runbooks/heal-credential-registry-drift.md.

droplet-uncommitted:main.plain_language_summary: The droplet git-drift healer found uncommitted file(s) on `main` whose newest edit is older than 6h (healer-managed runtime paths are excluded first). The healer is observation-only by design — it never auto-commits or discards — and it already DM'd you directly at emit time via route=escalate. This entry silences Pulse's Check-0 redundant re-triage of the same record (which was re-escalating it as a novel Tier-4 alert each cycle); it does NOT silence the primary healer DM, which still fires every 6h until the tree is clean. The raw subject carries the branch after the colon (droplet-uncommitted:<branch>); this key matches via the prefix-strip lookup rule. By-design dedup, not a failure.
droplet-uncommitted:main.recommended_action: Review the named files (the alert body lists them) and either commit or restore them: `cd /home/larry/agent-core && git status && git diff`. Once the working tree is clean the healer stops firing. This entry only mutes Pulse's duplicate re-escalation — the primary 6h healer DM still reaches you, so genuinely-new uncommitted drift on main is never hidden. Producer: scripts/heal_droplet_git_drift.py (observation-only).

chain-event-shipper-stale.plain_language_summary: The chain-event-shipper daemon has not posted a heartbeat in over its threshold. Mission-control dashboard is now showing stale data — the chain may or may not be moving, but you can't see it from the UI.
chain-event-shipper-stale.recommended_action: Run `sudo systemctl restart chain-event-shipper.service` and check `journalctl -u chain-event-shipper.service -n 50` for the underlying error. If the shipper crashes immediately on restart, inspect ~/agents/logs/chain_event_shipper.log for the stack trace.

summary.plain_language_summary: The hourly dispatch-branch GC backstop (ourliberty-cleanup-dispatch-branches.timer) ran and pruned stale Forge/Mirror dispatch branches — the routine housekeeping success path. It runs every hour and almost always has something small to prune, so it fires frequently by design. route=digest means it is already surfaced only in the daily CEO digest, never DM'd. By-design FYI, not a failure.
summary.recommended_action: None — by-design housekeeping confirmation. Per-run detail (how many local/remote branches pruned, any deferred by batch cap) is in the digest line and ~/agents/logs/cleanup_dispatch_branches.log. The sibling `gh-unavailable` subject is route=escalate and DOES still surface — only this routine `summary` is silenced.

gh-unavailable.plain_language_summary: The hourly dispatch-branch cleanup couldn't reach GitHub (`gh` unavailable) for one or more repos, so it SKIPPED pruning their stale Forge/Mirror branches this run. Nothing was deleted unsafely — without `gh` it can't check which branches still back an open PR (the guard against deleting a live branch), so it skips rather than risk it. Stale branches just keep piling up until `gh` works again. Unlike the routine `summary` this is route=escalate, because a persistent `gh` outage means the cleanup backstop is effectively dark.
gh-unavailable.recommended_action: Check `gh` on the droplet: `gh auth status`, then a probe like `gh pr list --repo Larry-Yatch/ourliberty-agent-core`. Re-auth with `gh auth login` if it's an auth failure (runbook: docs/runbooks/audit-github-gh-oauth.md); otherwise look for a network or rate-limit issue. Cleanup self-resumes on its next hourly run once `gh` is reachable. Per-repo detail is in ~/agents/logs/dispatch-branch-cleanup.log.

auto-merge-queue-corrupt.plain_language_summary: The auto-merge queue file at ~/agents/blackboard/auto-merge-queue.json failed to parse — JSON syntax error or structural surprise. The notifier has fail-closed: every subsequent auto-merge attempt is HELD until the file is repaired and the daemon restarts.
auto-merge-queue-corrupt.recommended_action: Inspect the file with `cat ~/agents/blackboard/auto-merge-queue.json` to find the corruption. Move it aside (`mv ... .broken`) to clear the queue, then `sudo systemctl restart outbox-notifier.service`. Recovery steps: runbooks/auto-merge-queue.md.

review-pass.plain_language_summary: Mirror approved a Forge-built PR and auto-merge fired — the routine build-completion success path (Mirror PASS -> squash-merge -> branch delete). No action required; the chain advanced as designed. This is a by-design FYI, not a failure.
review-pass.recommended_action: None — by-design success confirmation. The merge outcome (merged / already_merged) is in the closing DM; the audit trail is in ~/agents/logs/outbox-notifier.log under AUTO_MERGE lines.

mirror-dag-pass.plain_language_summary: Mirror's DAG preflight verification PASSED for a multi-step build sequence (no cycles, all depends_on references resolve, parallel steps touch no overlapping files, all referenced spec sections exist). The sequence auto-transitions pending -> active and the advancer dispatches the first step. The raw subject carries the sequence id after a colon (mirror-dag-pass:<seq-id>); this bare key matches via the prefix-strip lookup rule. By-design FYI, not a failure.
mirror-dag-pass.recommended_action: None — by-design success confirmation that a sequence kicked off cleanly. The sequence file is at ~/agents/blackboard/build-sequences/<seq-id>.json; advancer activity is in ~/agents/logs/outbox-notifier.log.

approval_request.plain_language_summary: Delivery confirmation: outbox-notifier successfully dispatched an APPROVAL_REQUEST Telegram DM to Larry. The approval is now awaiting Larry's response in beacon-pending-approvals.json. No action needed from Pulse — the DM was already delivered.
approval_request.recommended_action: None. The Telegram DM has already been delivered. Monitor ~/agents/state/beacon-pending-approvals.json for the pending item.

sequence-complete.plain_language_summary: A multi-step build sequence finished — its final step reached verified-merged and outbox-notifier emitted the completion summary. The notifier already delivers this directly to Larry via route=escalate (he gets the Telegram DM at emit time), so Pulse's Check 0 re-read of the same record would only duplicate it. The raw subject carries the sequence id after a colon (sequence-complete:<seq-id>); this bare key matches via the prefix-strip lookup rule. By-design FYI, not a failure.
sequence-complete.recommended_action: None — by-design success confirmation that a build sequence completed. The original completion DM was already delivered via the outbox-notifier route=escalate path; this entry only silences Pulse's redundant re-read. Sequence file: ~/agents/blackboard/build-sequences/<seq-id>.json; completion detail in ~/agents/logs/outbox-notifier.log under SEQUENCE_COMPLETE lines.

wedged-review-reaped.plain_language_summary: The wedged-review-session healer reaped an idle Forge/Mirror review session and removed its worktree — the routine self-heal success path. A review session sat idle past its threshold (commonly because a replan/retry task superseded the original review), so the healer killed the stale process tree and cleaned up the worktree. By-design FYI, not a failure. The raw subject carries the worktree name after a colon (wedged-review-reaped:<wt-name>); this bare key matches via the prefix-strip lookup rule.
wedged-review-reaped.recommended_action: None — by-design success confirmation that a wedged review session was reaped and its worktree cleaned up. Audit trail: the HEALED lines in ~/agents/logs/heal-wedged-review-sessions.log. Runbook: runbooks/heal-wedged-review-sessions.md.

wedged-review-silent.plain_language_summary: The wedged-review-session healer spotted a Forge/Mirror review session idle past its threshold with no terminal marker, but is in alert-only mode (Case 2 not yet graduated) so it did NOT kill it. Unlike wedged-review-reaped, nothing was healed — this is a heads-up that a review session may be genuinely stuck and needs an operator to look. Common benign cause: the PR already merged, making the review moot while the session lingers. Common real cause: a poll-loop / inbox-watcher wedge holding the session open. The raw subject carries the worktree name after a colon (wedged-review-silent:<wt-name>); this bare key matches via the prefix-strip lookup rule.
wedged-review-silent.recommended_action: Look before killing. Inspect the worktree (`ls -la ~/agent-worktrees/<wt-name>`) and the session log named in the alert. Check whether the session's PR already merged (`gh pr view`) — if so the review is moot and the session is safe to kill. If genuinely wedged, kill the claude PID named in the alert; inbox-watcher will retry harmlessly. If a bash poll loop is spinning (pgrep-empty → /proc check always true → until-loop never exits), that's the root cause — fix the loop's liveness check, don't just kill the symptom. Runbook: runbooks/heal-wedged-review-sessions.md.

wedged-review-case2-graduated.plain_language_summary: The wedged-review-session healer's Case-2 (silent, no-terminal-marker sessions) confidence streak crossed the promotion threshold, so it graduated from alert-only to auto-reap. From now on it will reap genuinely-wedged silent sessions automatically instead of only alerting (wedged-review-silent). By-design milestone confirmation, not a failure — the inverse event (a false positive demoting it back to alert-only) is logged as DEMOTED but not alerted.
wedged-review-case2-graduated.recommended_action: None — by-design confirmation that Case-2 auto-reap is now active after enough consecutive correct alerts. If you'd rather it stay alert-only, lower the confidence or reset the streak per runbooks/heal-wedged-review-sessions.md.

wedged-review-verdict-undelivered.plain_language_summary: A wedged Mirror review actually finished with a real verdict, but that verdict was NEVER posted to the PR, and the reaper could not auto-deliver it (either it couldn't extract the marker or the delivery write failed). The healer killed the stuck process but PRESERVED the worktree so the verdict is not lost. Net effect: a PR is sitting with a completed-but-unposted review — the chain is stalled on that PR until someone recovers the verdict by hand. The subject carries the worktree name after the colon (wedged-review-verdict-undelivered:<wt-name>).
wedged-review-verdict-undelivered.recommended_action: Recover the verdict by hand. Open the preserved worktree and the session log named in the alert body, read off the Mirror verdict (pass / revision / escalate), and re-post the PR review or merge accordingly. The wedged process is already killed and the worktree is intentionally NOT removed — do not delete it until the verdict is recovered. Runbook: runbooks/heal-wedged-review-sessions.md.

bots:pulse:tmux.plain_language_summary: Pulse-bot is running via tmux (the intended deployment after PR #161). No action needed unless the tmux session is also down.
bots:pulse:tmux.recommended_action: If you want to verify or relaunch: `tmux has-session -t pulse-bot` to check, `bash ~/agent-core/scripts/pulse_telegram_bot.sh` to (re)launch into the same tmux session. Do NOT run `sudo systemctl restart ourliberty-pulse-bot.service` — that would start a second pulse-bot instance competing with tmux for getUpdates.

bots:pulse:down.plain_language_summary: Pulse-bot is DOWN: both the tmux session and the systemd unit failed liveness checks. No Telegram pulse-side traffic is flowing.
bots:pulse:down.recommended_action: Relaunch the intended tmux deployment: `bash ~/agent-core/scripts/pulse_telegram_bot.sh`. Verify with `tmux has-session -t pulse-bot && tmux capture-pane -p -t pulse-bot | tail -20`. Runbook: runbooks/watchdog-bot-policy.md.

bots:beacon:down.plain_language_summary: Beacon-bot is DOWN and the auto-restart carve-out also failed. Telegram alert delivery itself is broken — DMs cannot reach you until beacon-bot is back.
bots:beacon:down.recommended_action: Run `sudo systemctl status ourliberty-beacon-bot.service && sudo journalctl -u ourliberty-beacon-bot.service -n 50` to find the failure mode, then `sudo systemctl restart ourliberty-beacon-bot.service`. Runbook: runbooks/watchdog-bot-policy.md.

bots:forge:down.plain_language_summary: Forge-bot is DOWN and systemd has not recovered it — StartLimitBurst (10 starts / 300s) likely exhausted. Forge tasks queued in the inbox will not be picked up.
bots:forge:down.recommended_action: Run `sudo systemctl status ourliberty-forge-bot.service && sudo systemctl restart ourliberty-forge-bot.service`. Check `journalctl -u ourliberty-forge-bot.service -n 50` for the underlying crash cause. Runbook: runbooks/watchdog-bot-policy.md.

bots:mirror:down.plain_language_summary: Mirror-bot is DOWN and systemd has not recovered it — StartLimitBurst likely exhausted. PR reviews queued for mirror will not run.
bots:mirror:down.recommended_action: Run `sudo systemctl status ourliberty-mirror-bot.service && sudo systemctl restart ourliberty-mirror-bot.service`. Check `journalctl -u ourliberty-mirror-bot.service -n 50` for the underlying crash cause. Runbook: runbooks/watchdog-bot-policy.md.

claude_tier1_failed_on_resume_session_bo.plain_language_summary: A Beacon chat turn failed mid-session and could not auto-retry on the backup (Tier 2) account, because Claude session IDs are tied to one account. Beacon itself stays running — only that one turn failed. Most often the underlying cause is a brief Anthropic server-side throttle (HTTP 429, 'not your usage limit') that clears on its own, NOT a real quota or auth problem.
claude_tier1_failed_on_resume_session_bo.recommended_action: First just send a fresh Beacon message — it starts a new (non-resumed) session and routes normally, which usually confirms recovery on its own. Only if the fresh message ALSO fails, probe `claude -p --output-format json 'say ok'` under each tier HOME (Tier 1: /home/larry; Tier 2: /home/larry/.claude-larry-personal) to tell apart a real auth-401 (re-login needed) from a usage-cap (wait for the rolling-5h window). NOTE: the raw alert's 'wait for the 5h window' advice is often wrong — the classifier currently mislabels transient 429s as auth_401 (fix queued).

claude_tier1_failed_tier2_unavailable.plain_language_summary: A dispatch failed on its active tier and could not fall back to the other tier (often a resume-bound session). Since #435 a session_lost is auto-recovered by a fresh re-dispatch; this alert now indicates a REAL tier failure — check the quota-events raw_excerpt before acting.
claude_tier1_failed_tier2_unavailable.recommended_action: Check ~/agents/blackboard/anthropic-quota-events.jsonl (the failing tier's raw_excerpt) before acting: a genuine rate_limit waits out the rolling-5h window on its own; an auth_401 needs re-auth via scripts/auth_orchestrator.py (Tier 1) or Tier 2 provisioning per docs/runbooks/restore-larry-personal-claude-oauth-tier2.md. A resume-bound session is marked paused_on_tier1 in the in-flight state file and will NOT auto-recover — re-dispatch once the tier is healthy.

claude_tier1_failed_tier2_unavailable.plain_language_summary: A dispatch failed on its active tier and could not fall back to the other tier (often a resume-bound session). Since #435 a session_lost is auto-recovered by a fresh re-dispatch; this alert now indicates a REAL tier failure — check the quota-events raw_excerpt before acting.

claude_max_5h_burn_threshold_breached.plain_language_summary: The trailing-5h Tier 1 quota-consuming token volume (input + output + cache_creation, from costs.jsonl; cache_read excluded) crossed 80% of the configured pace gate (tier1_quota.max_5h_token_threshold). This is a leading proxy for the real rolling-5h Anthropic rate-limit window — heads-up that sustained pace will hit the wall if it continues. No money is involved (OAuth Max has no per-token billing); the prior dollar framing was retired 2026-05-28.
claude_max_5h_burn_threshold_breached.recommended_action: Decide whether to pause dispatches or let the rolling-5h window cycle out. For ground-truth quota state, check https://console.anthropic.com/settings/usage; for the actual rate-limit-event log, see ~/agents/blackboard/anthropic-quota-events.jsonl. The threshold is auto-tuned weekly by scripts/pulse_check_viii.py against precision/recall on the event ledger — don't hand-tune.

tier2_provisioning_drift.plain_language_summary: Tier 2 (the fallback Claude account) is not at capability parity with Tier 1, so if work rotates to Tier 2 the agent runs degraded. Authentication is fine -- this is about the surrounding provisioning: a missing MCP server (the agent silently loses those tools), or a session-running systemd unit that no longer carves the Tier-2 home into ReadWritePaths (Tier-2 transcripts hit EROFS and --resume fails, silently losing the session). The weekly Tier-2 probe now checks this; the raw alert lists exactly which facet drifted.
tier2_provisioning_drift.recommended_action: Read the drift list in the raw message and bring Tier 2 to parity per docs/runbooks/tier1-tier2-switch-capability-audit.md. MCP gap: define the server in a project .mcp.json (tier-proof) or authenticate it under TIER2_HOME. ReadWritePaths gap: add TIER2_HOME to the unit ReadWritePaths and reinstall via the install-drift healer. This is SOON not NOW -- Tier 1 is healthy; the risk only materializes on a rotation to Tier 2.

tier2_weekly_probe_failed.plain_language_summary: The backup (Tier 2) OAuth account failed its weekly health probe — the automatic failover safety net may be down. The primary (Tier 1) account is unaffected, but if Tier 1 ever hits its limit there would be no working fallback.
tier2_weekly_probe_failed.recommended_action: Re-auth Tier 2 per docs/runbooks/restore-larry-personal-claude-oauth-tier2.md. Manual re-probe: `HOME=/home/larry/.claude-larry-personal claude -p --model claude-opus-4-7 'say ok'` — a clean 'ok' means Tier 2 is healthy again.

sync-blocked.plain_language_summary: ourliberty-sync refused to fast-forward main from origin. The working tree on the VM is not receiving PR merges until the underlying block is cleared.
sync-blocked.recommended_action: ssh ourliberty-vm, `cd ~/agent-core && git status` to see the gating condition. Most common causes: uncommitted modifications, wrong branch checkout, divergence with origin. Resolve per the more-specific subject (uncommitted-changes / wrong-branch / fast-forward-failed).

sync-blocked:uncommitted-changes.plain_language_summary: ourliberty-sync refused to pull because ~/agent-core has uncommitted modifications. Commonly Pulse runtime files (cycle-journal, cycle-actions, MEMORY) left dirty by an interactive /cycle — those should now auto-commit; anything else is human-touched dirt.
sync-blocked:uncommitted-changes.recommended_action: ssh ourliberty-vm, `cd ~/agent-core && git status` to identify the dirty files. If they are Pulse-owned, commit + push manually; otherwise commit/stash the human work. Sync resumes on the next tick once the tree is clean.

sync-blocked:wrong-branch.plain_language_summary: ourliberty-sync refused to pull because ~/agent-core is checked out on a non-main branch. Per the ourliberty-agent-core operating model, all work commits direct to main; a feature branch on the VM is unexpected.
sync-blocked:wrong-branch.recommended_action: ssh ourliberty-vm, `cd ~/agent-core`, `git checkout main`, and merge or discard the feature branch as appropriate. Then sync will resume on the next tick.

sync-blocked:fast-forward-failed.plain_language_summary: ourliberty-sync tried to fast-forward main from origin/main and failed — the local repo and origin have diverged. The chain stops receiving PR merges until the divergence is resolved.
sync-blocked:fast-forward-failed.recommended_action: ssh ourliberty-vm, `cd ~/agent-core`, run `git log --oneline origin/main..HEAD` to see what is local-only, then rebase or hard-reset to origin/main once it is safe to drop the local commits.

sync-blocked:validation-failed.plain_language_summary: ourliberty-sync pulled a new commit from origin/main but validate_agent_core.py rejected it; the sync rolled back to the previous HEAD. The tree is consistent but stuck behind origin until the bad commit is fixed upstream.
sync-blocked:validation-failed.recommended_action: ssh ourliberty-vm, `cd ~/agent-core`, `git checkout <new-head>`, then `python3 scripts/validate_agent_core.py` to see what failed. Fix on origin/main; the next sync tick will pick it up.

sync-blocked:quiescence-timeout.plain_language_summary: ourliberty-sync ran with REQUIRE_QUIESCENCE=1 and the strict-quiescence wait exceeded its timeout; sync rolled back. A non-quiescent agent kept the tree from being safely swapped.
sync-blocked:quiescence-timeout.recommended_action: ssh ourliberty-vm, `cd ~/agent-core && python3 scripts/await_quiescence.py` to identify the busy agent(s). Resolve before the next sync tick (or let sync run without REQUIRE_QUIESCENCE if soft-quiescence is acceptable).

deploy-restart-storm.plain_language_summary: ourliberty-sync.service detected a widely-imported module change after a PR merge and restarted the dependent daemons (typically 6-8) so they pick up the new code. This restart storm is the expected, self-healing deploy mechanism — it is how a code change propagates to running daemons, not a fault. route=digest confirms the system is healthy.
deploy-restart-storm.recommended_action: None — the multi-daemon restart is the deploy completing successfully. If individual daemons fail to come back healthy AFTER a restart storm (distinct from the storm itself), the per-daemon healer alerts surface that separately. Producer: ourliberty-sync.service post-merge deploy hook.

cycle-tier-corrupted.plain_language_summary: The cycle-tier state file was missing or had an invalid schema, so the system reset it to the Tier 1 defaults and kept running. Nothing is stuck, but a recurrence means something keeps corrupting that file.
cycle-tier-corrupted.recommended_action: One-off: no action needed, it self-recovered. If it recurs, inspect ~/agents/state/cycle-tier.json by hand for what is writing bad data.

summary.plain_language_summary: missions-autoregister periodically scans orphan threads and proposes auto-registration for the best candidate. This is routine housekeeping — the result is a committed thread proposal with route=digest. No operator action required.
summary.recommended_action: None. The autoregister healer handles this automatically. Review the proposed thread in ~/agent-core/agents/ if the proposal looks unexpected.

failure.plain_language_summary: missions-autoregister proposed orphan-thread registrations (and/or ingested new-mission PRs) but couldn't commit and push the result to main — the subject suffix names the git problem (`wrong-branch`, `commit-failed`, or `push-failed`). The work was computed but didn't persist, so the Missions board won't reflect the new proposals until a later clean run lands them.
failure.recommended_action: Check the droplet repo state (`cd ~/agent-core && git status`) — a non-main checkout or a dirty/diverged tree is the usual cause; the change is retained locally and the next run retries. Detail is in ~/agents/logs/missions-autoregister.log around the alert time.

proposed:needs-decision.plain_language_summary: One or more Proposed cards have sat on the Missions board past the 14-day grace with no matching shipped/closed PR, so the autoregister healer can neither auto-retire them (no terminal-PR evidence) nor leave them silent. They are flagged `needs_decision` and surfaced here, low-noise via route=digest, for you to keep or drop. These are typically closeout deferred-work notes or orphan cards whose task_id never mapped to a branch — genuine backlog needing a human call, not a failure.
proposed:needs-decision.recommended_action: Open the Missions tab's Proposed lane and, for each flagged card, dismiss it (drop) if the work is done/moot or accept it (keep) if it's still worth building. No urgency — they stay parked until you decide. The exact ids are in the digest line and ~/agents/logs/missions-autoregister.log.

failure.plain_language_summary: The missions-card garbage collector (it retires stale desktop-session cards and ages out old parked captures, then commits captures.json) computed its cleanup but couldn't fully land it. The subject suffix names which: `wrong-branch`, `commit-failed`, or `push-failed` is a git problem persisting the captures.json change; otherwise one or more card-retirement events failed to emit. Stale cards may linger on the Missions board until a later clean run.
failure.recommended_action: Grep ~/agents/logs/missions-card-gc.log around the alert time for the exact git/emit error. For a wrong-branch / commit / push failure, check the droplet repo state (`cd ~/agent-core && git status`) — the captures.json change is retained locally and the next GC run retries. For emit-failures the affected card ids are in the alert body; verify Supabase / chain_event_emit health.

check-iv-update.plain_language_summary: The weekly marker-drift check found Mirror's marker shape is drifting often enough to propose tightening enforcement (prompt re-emphasis or a hard validator gate). This is a proposal awaiting your call, not a failure.
check-iv-update.recommended_action: Review the proposal and reply `approve check-iv-update-<date>` or `reject check-iv-update-<date> <reason>` on Telegram. No action keeps the current enforcement unchanged.

check-v-update.plain_language_summary: The Tier-1 action-template trust check proposes changes to the guard list: graduating templates that have earned trust, or adding ones that triggered a correction. This is a proposal awaiting your call, not a failure.
check-v-update.recommended_action: Review the proposals and reply `approve check-v-update-<date>` or `reject check-v-update-<date> <reason>` on Telegram. No action leaves the guard list as-is.

check-vi-update.plain_language_summary: The PRIME DIRECTIVE posture check proposes tuning the verification-pending handling (auto-promote window or stuck-forever thresholds) based on the last 30 days. This is a proposal awaiting your call, not a failure.
check-vi-update.recommended_action: Review the proposals and reply `approve check-vi-update-<date>` or `reject check-vi-update-<date> <reason>` on Telegram. No action leaves the current posture unchanged.

rotation_auth_gate_blocked.plain_language_summary: The scheduler tried to rotate the active Claude account into the next tier but that tier's OAuth credentials are missing, expired, or unverifiable, so it held on the current tier. The chain still moves on the held tier; it will retry the flip after you re-auth.
rotation_auth_gate_blocked.recommended_action: Re-auth the blocked tier so the next rotation window can flip. Runbook: docs/runbooks/restore-larry-personal-claude-oauth-tier2.md.

check-viii-update.plain_language_summary: The marker precision/recall floor check proposes raising, lowering, or deprecating a validation threshold based on the last week. A deprecate proposal is the strongest variant. This is a proposal awaiting your call, not a failure.
check-viii-update.recommended_action: Review the proposal and reply `approve check-viii-update-<date>` or `reject check-viii-update-<date> <reason>` on Telegram. No action leaves the current floors unchanged.

check-viii-defer.plain_language_summary: The marker precision/recall floor check could not auto-propose because both precision and recall fell below their floors this week, so it needs you to read the artifact and decide whether to raise, lower, or hold.
check-viii-defer.recommended_action: Read the week's artifact and decide manually whether to raise, lower, or hold the floors. No automated proposal applies here.

check-x-regression.plain_language_summary: The weekly chain-quality watch found that since the last model/prompt cutover, the Forge/Mirror build chain has gotten measurably harder on at least one quality signal (Forge needs more clarification rounds per task, or more build/revision rounds per task). This is CORRELATIONAL — the cutover happens to coincide with the rise; it is not proven cause. It is a heads-up awaiting your call, not an automated change.
check-x-regression.recommended_action: Review the recent Forge/Mirror PRs from the trailing window (the DM names the metric and shows the before -> after numbers). If the regression looks real, revert the affected agent to claude-opus-4-7 by flipping its routing value in config/agent-models.json and restarting the inbox-watcher (it caches config at startup, inbox_watcher.py:778). No automated action is taken; the full metric table is in ~/agents/blackboard/pulse-check-x-proposals/check-x-<Monday>.json.

pulse-check-xii-monthly-digest.plain_language_summary: The monthly delivery-effectiveness digest (Check XII) — a plain-language readout of how the factory delivered over the trailing 4 weeks: merges (mission-linked vs unlinked), dispatch-to-merge lead time, and cost per mission shipped. This is observe-only: Check XII has NO firing rules yet, so this is a baseline snapshot for calibration, not an alert about anything wrong.
pulse-check-xii-monthly-digest.recommended_action: No action required — this is an informational baseline. The full metric table (throughput split, lead time, rework, survival, cost, demand) is in ~/agents/blackboard/pulse-check-xii/. Read it if you want the delivery picture; the numbers are what V1.1's firing rules will eventually calibrate against.

pulse-check-xii-source-dark.plain_language_summary: One of Check XII's four data sources (github / chain_events / costs / missions) has failed to load for 2 consecutive weekly runs, so the delivery metrics that depend on it are reporting insufficient_signal instead of real numbers. A single run's blip is suppressed by design; two in a row means it is not self-resolving. The subject carries the dark source name after the colon.
pulse-check-xii-source-dark.recommended_action: Investigate the named source before the next Monday firing. github = the `gh` CLI / auth; chain_events + missions = Supabase reachability/credentials; costs = ~/agents/blackboard cost ledger. Run `python3 ~/agent-core/scripts/pulse_check_xii.py --dry-run` to see which source raises and why; the artifact's `sources` block records per-source status.

pulse-check-xii-rule.plain_language_summary: A Check XII delivery-effectiveness firing rule has tripped: a delivery metric moved past its calibrated threshold over the trailing window. This is a V1.1+ signal (V1 is observe-only, so it does not fire yet). The subject carries the rule number after the colon.
pulse-check-xii-rule.recommended_action: Review the named metric's before -> after numbers in the DM and the full table in ~/agents/blackboard/pulse-check-xii/. The rule is a heads-up about a delivery-throughput/quality/cost shift, not an automated change — decide whether it reflects a real regression worth acting on.

cycle-blocked.plain_language_summary: A Pulse maintenance cycle was stopped by its branch-guard because ~/agent-core was not on a clean main checkout, so it refused to auto-commit the cycle journal onto the wrong branch. Read the subject to tell the two cases apart: 'dirty-tree-on-<branch>' is expected-by-design and self-resolves once the working tree returns to main (no action needed); 'auto-restore-failed-from-<branch>' means the automatic return-to-main failed and needs a manual fix.
cycle-blocked.recommended_action: If the subject is dirty-tree-on-*, no action is required -- the next cycle runs once ~/agent-core is back on a clean main. If it is auto-restore-failed-from-*, ssh ourliberty-vm, cd ~/agent-core, and manually restore a clean main checkout (origin may have diverged); cycles resume on the next tick.

cycle:stray-tree-edit-reverted.plain_language_summary: The Pulse /cycle agent edited a tracked file in the live repo OUTSIDE its own runtime paths (e.g. config/alert-translations.json) -- an out-of-contract change that, left uncommitted, would have wedged ourliberty-sync + agent-core-health and paged you every ~30 min (the 2026-06-26 class). run_cycle.sh's clean-tree guard auto-reverted it (the diff is archived under ~/agents/logs/stray-cycle-edits-*.diff first, so nothing is lost) and surfaced this FYI. The live tree is clean; no action needed. Governed config/code changes are supposed to flow through a Forge PR, not be hand-applied to live.
cycle:stray-tree-edit-reverted.recommended_action: None -- self-healed: the stray edit was reverted and archived. If the change was actually wanted, route it through a Forge PR (the reviewed, approved channel). If this fires repeatedly, the cycle prompt's Check A discipline needs reinforcing -- check the archived diffs to see what Pulse keeps trying to write.

*.plain_language_summary: This is one of Pulse's own cycle-emitted escalations being re-read by Check 0 on the next cycle -- a self-echo. Every source=pulse-cycle record is, by construction, Pulse's own outbound emission (a [yellow]/[red] it appended to larry-alerts.jsonl), and the original already reached Larry at emit time via the beacon-bot alert sweep. On the next cycle Check 0 re-reads that record and would otherwise classify it as a fresh novel alert. This catch-all silences the re-read so it stays journal-only. More-specific pulse-cycle subjects (e.g. cycle-blocked) still match their own entry first. Genuinely-important findings (e.g. unreviewed merges) also surface independently via their own detector source, so silencing the echo here drops no real signal.
*.recommended_action: No action required. This is by-design self-echo suppression: the original escalation already reached Larry at emit time, and this entry only mutes Pulse's re-read of its own outbound record on the following cycle.

push-soft-validate-failed.plain_language_summary: The pre-push soft validator (validate_agent_core.py) flagged an error on the commit that was about to push to origin/main. This is a SOFT gate -- the push was NOT blocked, so the commit went through; this is a review-when-convenient signal, not a chain stop. The subject carries the short SHA of the flagged commit.
push-soft-validate-failed.recommended_action: ssh ourliberty-vm, cd ~/agent-core, run `python3 scripts/validate_agent_core.py` to see what the validator flagged. Duplicate failures with the same fingerprint are suppressed, so a repeat means a new or changed failure. Fix on origin/main when convenient.

inbox-stall.plain_language_summary: Sentinel detected an inbox task waiting longer than the stale threshold. This is expected during Tier 2 OAuth expiry -- agent processing is blocked and tasks accumulate. Beacon-bot delivers the DM, but no new action is needed beyond what is already pending.
inbox-stall.recommended_action: None. The task is waiting because agent processing is OAuth-blocked. Root cause: restore Tier 2 OAuth per docs/runbooks/restore-larry-personal-claude-oauth-tier2.md. Tasks will process automatically once OAuth is restored.

pulse-check-stale.plain_language_summary: A Pulse self-optimization check (I-X) has gone dark: its last success heartbeat is older than its expected cadence + grace, so it has silently stopped firing. The check itself is usually healthy -- the failure is in whatever is supposed to invoke it (the Pulse /cycle). This is exactly the failure that hid the IX/X stall for ~2 days. The subject carries the check id after the colon.
pulse-check-stale.recommended_action: Run `python3 ~/agent-core/scripts/pulse_check_<id>.py` to confirm the check exits 0 (it usually does), then investigate why the Pulse /cycle stopped invoking it. Heartbeats live at ~/agents/blackboard/pulse-check-<id>.heartbeat; cadences are in config/pulse-check-cadence.json; check logs are under ~/agents/logs/pulse-check-*.log.

pulse-check-no-cadence.plain_language_summary: The liveness watcher found a Pulse check it knows about that has no (or a malformed) entry in config/pulse-check-cadence.json, so that check's liveness is not being monitored. Fail-closed: it alerts rather than leaving the check silently unwatched. The subject carries the check id after the colon.
pulse-check-no-cadence.recommended_action: Add (or fix) a cadence_hours + grace_hours entry -- or an event_driven entry -- for the named check id in config/pulse-check-cadence.json, following the existing entries' shape.

pulse-check-config-unreadable.plain_language_summary: config/pulse-check-cadence.json could not be loaded (missing or invalid JSON), so the pulse-check liveness watcher is monitoring nothing until it is fixed. The watchers are unwatched.
pulse-check-config-unreadable.recommended_action: Validate the file with `python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('config/pulse-check-cadence.json'))"` and repair the JSON. The watcher resumes on its next OnCalendar run once the file parses.

pulse-check-failed.plain_language_summary: A Pulse self-optimization check (I-X) ran but did not complete cleanly (it raised or exited nonzero), so it did NOT refresh its liveness heartbeat. This is the same-cycle complement to the staleness watcher -- it names the failing check immediately instead of waiting out the staleness window. The subject carries the check id after the colon.
pulse-check-failed.recommended_action: Run `python3 ~/agent-core/scripts/pulse_check_<id>.py` by hand and read the traceback; logs are under ~/agents/logs/pulse-check-*.log. Fix the underlying error so the check resumes emitting heartbeats.

catalog-accuracy-drift.plain_language_summary: The shelf catalog-accuracy meter (in ourliberty-graph) found that some reusable-component shelf cards no longer verify against live code — their recorded facts (dependents, seams) have moved since the card was characterized. A drifted card can mislead component reuse, but nothing in the build chain is broken. Maintenance-grade, surfaced in the daily digest only (route=digest), never DM'd. The drifted card ids and the attention-rate-vs-gate numbers are in the alert body.
catalog-accuracy-drift.recommended_action: No urgency. When convenient, re-characterize the drifted cards in ourliberty-graph: `./pipeline/regen_descriptor.sh <id>` (or `batch_catalog.sh` for several), then commit and re-run `pipeline/accuracy_meter.py` to confirm the attention rate is back under the gate. The drifted ids are named in the alert body.

beacon-erofs.plain_language_summary: Pulse detected the Beacon (or another claude-subprocess) bot returning [claude exit 1] because the claude CLI hit EROFS when writing /home/larry/.claude.json. Root cause: ProtectHome=read-only in the systemd unit whitelists the .claude/ directory but not the home-root .claude.json file. The CLI rewrites this file on some turns (startup-count bump, cache-TTL refresh, new project entry) — only those turns fail, making it intermittent. PR #470 (2026-06-11) added the file to ReadWritePaths on all 18 claude-invoking units; live drop-ins bridge the gap until those inline units are reinstalled.
beacon-erofs.recommended_action: 1) Verify drop-ins are in place: `ls /etc/systemd/system/ourliberty-{beacon,forge,mirror,pulse,cycle,ledger,*}-bot.service.d/claude-json-writable.conf` — if any are missing, re-apply via `sudo mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/<unit>.service.d && printf '[Service]\nReadWritePaths=/home/larry/.claude.json\n' | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/<unit>.service.d/claude-json-writable.conf && sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart <unit>`. 2) Verify PR #470 is in the installed units: `grep .claude.json /etc/systemd/system/ourliberty-cycle.service` — if absent the install-drift healer hasn't converged yet, keep the drop-ins. 3) Once inline units are installed (grep returns the path), clean up all drop-ins: `sudo rm /etc/systemd/system/ourliberty-*.service.d/claude-json-writable.conf && sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo systemctl restart ourliberty-beacon-bot ourliberty-forge-bot ourliberty-mirror-bot ourliberty-pulse-bot`. Runbook: see PR #470 and the claude-json-erofs-readwrite memory entry.

check-i.plain_language_summary: Pulse's Check I weekly cost digest — the rolling-window spend/usage report it emits once a week. Pulse already delivers this to Larry directly via route=escalate (he gets the beacon-bot DM at emit time), so Pulse's Check 0 re-read of the same record on the next cycle would only duplicate it. The raw subject carries the rotating report date after a hyphen (check-i-<YYYY-MM-DD>); this stable key matches via the trailing-ISO-date-strip lookup rule. By-design FYI, not a failure.
check-i.recommended_action: None — by-design weekly cost report. The Check I digest already reached you via route=escalate at emit time; this entry only silences Pulse's redundant Check-0 re-triage of the same record. The narrow 'check-i' key plus the date-strip means only this weekly digest is muted — every other source=pulse escalation (e.g. beacon-erofs, unreviewed-merge) still surfaces.

weekly.plain_language_summary: The weekly cost-ledger report — the five-section spend/usage rollup the ledger emits once a week. The producer already delivers this to Larry directly via route=escalate (he gets the beacon-bot DM at emit time), so Pulse's Check 0 re-read of the same record on the next cycle would only duplicate it. The raw subject carries the rotating report date after a hyphen (weekly-<YYYY-MM-DD>); this stable key matches via the trailing-ISO-date-strip lookup rule. By-design FYI, not a failure.
weekly.recommended_action: None — by-design; the weekly ledger DM already reached you via route=escalate; this only mutes Pulse's duplicate re-read. The ledger is single-purpose (it only ever emits weekly-<date>), so this entry silences Pulse's redundant Check-0 re-triage without hiding any other signal. Report detail: weekly-YYYY-MM-DD.md from scripts/ledger_weekly.py.

unreviewed-merge.plain_language_summary: A pull request was merged into main with NO evidence of a Mirror REVIEW_PASS -- the Mirror-review merge gate did not hold for it. This is the exact hole that let #303 (merged despite a REVISION verdict) and #324 (merged with no review) slip through. Branch protection should now block this; if this alert fires, protection was bypassed or misconfigured. The subject carries the PR number after the colon.
unreviewed-merge.recommended_action: Inspect the merge with `gh pr view <N> --repo Larry-Yatch/ourliberty-agent-core`. If it should not have merged, assess the change and revert if needed. Confirm branch protection is intact: `gh api repos/Larry-Yatch/ourliberty-agent-core/branches/main/protection`. This is a defense-in-depth detector; treat a hit as a gate failure worth root-causing.

undispatched-pr-review.plain_language_summary: An open Forge PR has no Mirror review, and the GitHub-truth backstop healer tried to dispatch one but it did not take (the review task is still absent after the dispatch attempt). The happy path here is silent -- the healer normally just dispatches the missed review and logs it; this alert only fires when the dispatch itself keeps failing (e.g. routing denied, missing target_repo), which means a PR will sit unreviewed until a human intervenes. This is the open-PR analogue of the unreviewed-merge detector and the durable fix for the #412 incident (a reaped build session left a clean PR with no review and no local outbox for the outbox-based reconcile to find). The subject carries the PR number after the colon.
undispatched-pr-review.recommended_action: Inspect why the Mirror review-request write is failing: grep the outbox-notifier log (~/agents/logs/outbox-notifier.log) for a 'review-request dispatch FAILED' / RoutingDenied / 'no target_repo' line referencing the task. Re-dispatch manually by writing a review task to ~/agents/inboxes/mirror/, and `gh pr view <N> --repo Larry-Yatch/ourliberty-agent-core` to confirm the PR state.

routing-denied.plain_language_summary: An inbox envelope was dropped to <agent>/.invalid because the layer-2 routing table denied its (source -> target) pair, even though it passed layer-1 source validation. A control surface lost this action silently -- its API call may have returned success while the work was discarded. This is the standing tripwire for the 2026-05-28 dashboard gap (dashboard Approve/Reject envelopes passed source validation but had no FRESH_DISPATCH_ROUTES entry). The subject carries the source->target route after the colon; the body carries the dropped envelope id. No auto-replay -- the envelope is gone, not retried.
routing-denied.recommended_action: Check whether the source legitimately should reach the target. If yes, add the route to routing_validator.FRESH_DISPATCH_ROUTES (the test_dispatch_route_parity guard exists for exactly this) and re-issue the dropped action manually (its id is in the alert body). If the denial is correct (a genuinely unlisted source), no action -- the alert confirms the gate held. Look in ~/agents/inboxes/<agent>/.invalid/ for the dropped envelope and its .reason sidecar.

tier-pool-all-unavailable.plain_language_summary: No dispatch tier is currently available, so new work is holding in the inbox instead of starting. Every tier is in cooldown or otherwise blocked (the alert body names the per-tier reason). This usually self-clears the moment any tier frees up — dispatches resume automatically. It only needs attention if it persists, which points at a stuck rotation or every tier hitting quota at once.
tier-pool-all-unavailable.recommended_action: First confirm it hasn't already cleared (new work resumes on its own when a tier frees). If it's persisting, inspect the live tier state with `cat ~/agents/blackboard/active-tier.json` and read each tier's block reason from the alert body. To force progress, pin a healthy tier via the dashboard rotation control (set rotation mode to off with a pinned tier) — the same override the /rotation endpoint writes. No action if it has already recovered — the alert only fires after the pool has been fully held past the hold-alert threshold.

sync_agent_core: auto-commit push failed.plain_language_summary: sync_agent_core auto-committed Pulse runtime files but the push to origin/main failed and was rolled back; the working tree is consistent and sync retries the push on the next tick (~5 min). Routine self-healing transient - the companion sync.service digest alert (sync-blocked:auto-commit-push-failed) already covers it, so this escalate-route ourliberty-health duplicate needs no separate action.
sync_agent_core: auto-commit push failed.recommended_action: No action - self-heals on the next sync tick. If the failure persists across many ticks, the actionable signal is the sync.service sync-blocked digest, not this one.

review-ceiling-fit.plain_language_summary: The weekly Mirror review-ceiling fit-monitor digest (scripts/heal_review_ceiling_fit.py). A READ-ONLY reporter that recomputes the Mirror PR-review duration distribution (p50/p90/p95/p99/max), counts review_session_timeout ceiling firings and likely false-kills (fired-then-merged PRs), and reports whether the harness review ceiling (agent_runner.REVIEW_SESSION_CEILING_SECONDS, default 35min) is still right-sized -- with a recommended value. It NEVER mutates the ceiling and NEVER pages: this is a route=digest record surfaced in the CEO digest, not a DM. By-design FYI, not a failure.
review-ceiling-fit.recommended_action: None by default -- this is an observe-and-report digest. If it recommends RAISING the ceiling (HEADROOM_LOW: p95 creeping into the ceiling, or FALSE_KILL: a fired review whose PR later merged), that is a signal to consider bumping OL_REVIEW_SESSION_CEILING_SECONDS; the monitor does not auto-tune it. Detail: the digest body carries the distribution, headroom, firing count, false-kill count, and the recommendation line.
